title: Saying When
label: ch:ml-when
canDo: I can say that something happens on a named day or at a named hour, and ask what time it happens.

payoff.summary: From cold: two answers to "when", and which of the two takes an ending.
payoff.note: NO WORD IN THIS CHAPTER IS NEW, and that is the chapter. ML-A1-TIME-10 has stood open with the note 'the parts are all present -- days, hours, the -il suffix -- and are never assembled', and the parts half of that note is right while the SUFFIX half is wrong: Malayalam fixes a clock time with the DATIVE, not the locative, and the dative has been taught since chapter 6. The inventory note is corrected in this pass rather than worked around; that is the third stale note in seven tranches, and the standing rule to verify a note before scoping from it is what caught it. EVERY PIECE WAS VERIFIED AS OWNED BEFORE DRAFTING: mani (ML-C18-mani, 470), the dative -ikku and its landing on jOli (ML-C06-dative-ikku, 320), raNTu (ML-C93-counted, 3310), ethra (ML-C19-vayassu 480, ML-C34-codikkuka 760, ML-C81-dooram 2820, ML-C91-ethra-rupa 3220). THE ETHRA WITNESS LIST WAS WRONG TWICE, AND THE SECOND TIME WAS THE CORRECTION. The draft counted -- 'the third question you have asked with this word' -- and a sweep found ML-C19 and made it three named witnesses. Review then found ML-C34-codikkuka at 760, which drills ethra maNi?, 'what hour?', in its own practice: the learner has been able to ASK THE HOUR for 2,930 points. That is not a missing witness in a list, it is the lesson's thesis: the question half of this point was one ENDING short, not one phrase short. The lesson is rewritten around it -- ethra maNi is presented as ALREADY OWNED and the ending as the whole difference between 'what time is it' and 'at what time'. Two passes over the same sentence, and the count was wrong in both; naming witnesses does not help if the sweep that finds them is keyed on script and ML-C34 gives the phrase in ROMANIZATION ONLY, which is the HL-C402 failure again, the when-slot at the front of nyaan pOkuM (ML-C94-three-days, 3350), and innu/naaLe (ML-C94, 3330-3350). THE ONE GENUINELY NEW THING IS A JOINT: -kku on the hour, nothing at all on the day. NOT A SINGLE MALAYALAM TOKEN GAINS A FIRST OWNER HERE. All four content headwords are multi-word, which continuity.ts keeps whole, so no earlier use turns into a forward reference -- the trap recorded in lessons.d as 'a multi-word headword owns no single token'. That mattered most for thiNkaLaazhcha: chapter 10 prints all seven day-names in its table under a seven-word headword and owns none of them singly, so giving the word a one-word lesson would have converted chapter 10's own table into a forward reference. It is taught here as a USE, type grammar, inside a sentence. maNikku was the same question from the other side: the reader can already BUILD it from mani plus the chapter 6 ending, and lessons.d says a word the corpus can already build must not be introduced later as a word -- so the lesson is about the ending's third sense, not about a word. ROMANIZATIONS ARE COPIED FROM THE OWNING LESSON, not re-derived: raNTu from ML-C93-counted, ethra from ML-C81 and ML-C91 (both spell it ethra, not etra), nyaan pOkuM from ML-C94-three-days, and thiNkaLaazhcha from ML-C10-azhcha's own thiNkaL plus aazhcha -- which keeps ML-C10's older zh and th spellings rather than the more recent llla and t, because a learner meets the word in that table first and should meet the same spelling twice. THE CORPUS ROMANIZES WORD-FINAL CHANDRAKKALA TWO WAYS (jOlikku in chapter 6, raNTu in chapter 93) and this chapter does not resolve that; jOlikku is therefore quoted in SCRIPT ONLY so the two spellings never stand side by side on one page, and the inconsistency is filed rather than papered over. WHAT THE CHAPTER REFUSES TO CLAIM: that a day-name CANNOT take an ending. It can, for other jobs. The lesson says it does not NEED one for saying when, which is what the corpus teaches and what is true. ONE METRIC MOVES AND IT IS A DELIBERATE TRADE: atomMeasurementBlindLessons goes 9 -> 10, because ML-C102-day-and-hour is a synthesis lesson with an EMPTY introduces list and ramp.ts counts a lesson with no introduced atom as unmeasurable. That shape is the one lessons.d recommends -- a chapter's last lesson must not introduce an atom, or the atom can never be revisited -- so the blind count is what the recommended shape costs, recorded rather than engineered away. ONE LIMIT ON THE CLOSE: the point's label is copular ('it is on Monday, it is at three') and this chapter produces no copular sentence. It locates an event with a fronted adjunct, which is the ordinary Malayalam way; 'it is at two' needs -aaNu on the time phrase and is not taught here.
